items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Geechie Fields on trombone, Happy Caldwell on clarinet

ctx.x: And yourself. And those titles are "Each Day," "If Someone Would Only Love Me," "That Will Never Do," and "I'm Looking for a Little Bluebird." And the second session which is June 2, 1930, is Jelly Roll, again Ward Pinkett and another on trumpet, Geechie Fields on trombone, Happy Caldwell on clarinet, Joe Thomas on alto sax, Walter Thomas on clarinet and baritone, Lee Blair on banjo, Billy Taylor once again on bass, and you; and those are "Oil Well," two takes of "Load of Coal," and "Crazy Chords," and "Primrose…
Yeah, "Primrose Stomp." It rings a bell.

items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: Yeah. I'd taken them into masonry, Mark We Morris too.

ctx.x: Yeah. I'd taken them into masonry, Mark We Morris too. All them belonged to Harlem 4, deceased like W. C. Handy and Jimmy Rushing, Big Sid Catlett, Teddy Fields, Lucky Millinder, bunch of them. The musicians you were knowing in jazz at the game masters, like Henry G. Wharton. He came over there to Europe with the Musical Spillers, and he stayed and went to school over there. And he was master in 1945. Robert Robinson was master in 1946-47, '48. (Unintelligible) master in 1950. Then Johnson passed in 1955. Joe…
office down here on Broadway. He was master in 1960.
